claim: Graph-walk repairs, carrying the 0.18.1 hang fix forward: every active graph traversal now has a cycle guard (visited array), depth is capped at 2 (was 5), the bidirectional walk in navigate_locate is a valid single-recursive-reference CTE (the previous form failed at first execution on any fresh install), and the walk is seeded only when graph_proximity_weight > 0 — at the default weight no traversal runs at all. No recall-quality claim is made for the graph signal: the only ablation attempted (#88) was withdrawn as invalid (zero power by construction), see benchmarks/mem_ab_v3/ABLATION_88_WITHDRAWN.md.
criterion: 12-query hang probe all under 8s on a production-size corpus AND both upgrade chains produce body-hash parity with a fresh install AND latency of the guarded walk is not measurable at default weight

result.corpus: 9,424 lessons / 74,778 edges (isolated container, snapshot of production)
result.body_hash_parity: both chains identical to fresh 0.19.0 for every extension function

latency_note: The one part of the withdrawn ablation #88 that survives is its latency safety check, measured on 0.19.0 bodies: enabling the guarded walk (weight 0.2, depth 2) added no measurable latency (p50 delta -0.2 ms, 0 timeouts in 3,000 calls). That number is about cost, not benefit.

corrections.context: 0.17.0 and 0.18.0 shipped an unguarded, cycle-unprotected depth-5 walk that ran on every call and could hang recall_hybrid for tens of seconds (fixed in 0.18.1 for the 0.18 line; this release carries the fix into the 0.19 line, which had the cycle guard but not the weight guard in its active recall_hybrid).
